title: Multi-provider API passthrough for external models (MaaS)

steps.caption: Module 01 creation beat: the ExternalProvider is created from the console Import YAML editor and goes Ready immediately - the controller reconciles the endpoint and the apikey auth from the labeled provider secret.

details.label: Auth
details.value: apikey from the ipp-managed provider secret

steps.caption: The ExternalModel maps the client-facing model name claude-sonnet to the provider with the passthrough-eligible apiFormat: messages and path /v1/messages - Ready with its HTTPRoute created successfully.

Publishing to MaaS: the MaaSModelRef references kind ExternalModel and pairs with an active subscription - here it stays Pending, Awaiting governance pairing, until the subscription and auth policy exist. The video's honest pairing beat.
The MaaS subscription governs the external model: modelRefs lists claude-sonnet in p2w15-llm with a 100-token/1-minute limit - Active as soon as it is created.
The MaaS auth policy grants the user group access - Active with no conflicting AuthPolicies, completing the pairing: the Pending MaaSModelRef flips to Ready, Governed and runtime-healthy.

details.label: Conflict check
details.value: No conflicting AuthPolicies on MaaS-managed HTTPRoutes

details.label: Result
details.value: MaaSModelRef now Ready - Governed and runtime-healthy

steps.caption: MaaS governance in the dashboard: the p2w15-maas-external-demo subscription appears alongside the workshop subscriptions - all Active.

The payoff: the subscription's Models section lists the external model - claude-sonnet (target model claude-sonnet-4-20250514) in p2w15-llm with its token limit, exactly as the module 02 dashboard verification documents.

Honest drift: module 02's External models tab does not exist on RHOAI 3.5.1 - project p2w15-llm shows no deployed models, because the external model is governed through MaaS governance, not Model deployments. Never faked.

details.label: Module 02 arc
details.value: External models tab - drifted on RHOAI 3.5.1

details.label: Why
details.value: external models are governed via MaaS governance

steps.caption: MaaS API keys: keys minted from the dashboard are listed with their status, subscription, owner, and expiration - the keys used for the passthrough test are scoped to p2w15-maas-external-demo.

details.label: Columns
details.value: Status, Subscription, Owner, Created, Last used, Expires

details.label: Hygiene
details.value: key values are never displayed on screen

steps.caption: Creating a persistent key: a key needs a name, description, and the subscription that scopes it - the key will work only with models that belong to the selected subscription.

details.label: Scoping
details.value: works only with models in the selected subscription

steps.caption: Full arc verified: the external model is published, governed, and routable - a native Anthropic Messages request to /v1/messages on the gateway returns HTTP 200 with a content array and stop_reason end_turn (upstream: the documented in-cluster stand-in, success real, never faked).

details.label: Response
details.value: Anthropic Messages JSON: content array, stop_reason end_turn

details.label: Routing
details.value: gateway detects /v1/messages, matches apiFormat: messages, forwards unchanged

details.label: Auth
details.value: MaaS API key via Authorization: Bearer (gateway AuthPolicy rule)
